# Audio playback fixtures

These files cover every source format accepted by the Rust player. They are
short enough to stage on SPIFFS together for device playback tests and are not
included in the production SPIFFS image.

All fixtures contain the same synthetic 440 Hz mono tone. The source is 0.4
seconds of signed 16-bit little-endian PCM at 16 kHz, generated by FFmpeg's
`sine` source. No third-party recording is included.

| File | Codec or container | Sample rate |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `tone.aac` | AAC in ADTS | 16 kHz |
| `tone.amr` | AMR-NB at 12.2 kbps | 8 kHz |
| `tone.awb` | AMR-WB at 23.85 kbps | 16 kHz |
| `tone.flac` | FLAC | 16 kHz |
| `tone.m4a` | AAC in M4A | 16 kHz |
| `tone.mp3` | MP3 | 16 kHz |
| `tone.ogg` | Ogg/Vorbis | 16 kHz |
| `tone.opus` | Ogg/Opus | 48 kHz |
| `tone.pcm` | Raw signed 16-bit little-endian PCM | 16 kHz |
| `tone.ts` | AAC in MPEG transport stream | 16 kHz |
| `tone.wav` | Signed 16-bit PCM in WAV | 16 kHz |

The non-AMR files were generated with FFmpeg 6.1.1 using bit-exact muxing.
AMR-NB used `opencore-amr` 0.1.6 and AMR-WB used `vo-amrwbenc` 0.1.3. Two
independent generations produced the hashes recorded in `SHA256SUMS`.

Run the following before staging the fixtures for a hardware playback pass:

```sh
(
    cd tests/fixtures/audio
    sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
)
```

Device testing must play every file through both `spiffs://` and HTTP where
that source is supported. It must also exercise cancellation, synchronous
completion, repetition, and volume changes.
